question.leadin: Answer some questions about the 18th President of the United States.
question.text: Prior to becoming President, Grant served in this war that began in 1846, the year after the United States annexed Texas. This war was ended by the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.
question.clue: As a representative, Abraham Lincoln doubted the validity of this war via the Spot Resolutions, and a philosopher refused to support either slavery or this war by paying his poll tax, as noted in Civil Disobedience.

swap.leadin: This document originally contained 39 separate provisions, though only 10 were ratified.
swap.text: Name this set of 10 amendments added to the U.S. Constitution in 1791.
swap.clue: This document ratified in the Massachusetts Compromise was derided as a "parchment barrier" by James Madison, and William Douglas argued that its penumbra protected a "zone of privacy" in Griswold v Connecticut.

question.leadin: This court case established the concept of judicial review.
question.text: Name this court case where John Adams appointed the plaintiff to the position of federal justice of the peace in a midnight appointment, but Jefferson did not deliver the appointment.
question.answerHtml: Marbury v. Madison [or Madison v. Marbury; prompt on partial answer as neither name is uniquely identifying by itself]
question.clue: This case was brought by a midnight judge who was denied his writ of mandamus.

swap.leadin: Henry Clay urged this man to not resign his post as Secretary of State under John Tyler.
swap.text: Name this Northern statesman who, along with Clay and John C. Calhoun, made up a "great triumvirate."
swap.clue: This man declared that "there are those who love it" while defending his alma mater in Dartmouth College v. Woodward, and he lost his Senate seat after he defended the Compromise of 1850 in his Seventh of March speech.

question.leadin: William Strickland built this institution in a Greek Revival style for its President, Nicholas Biddle.
question.text: Name this national institution that was destroyed by the Distribution Act of 1836, which forced currency to be only gold and silver.
question.answer: Second Bank of the United States
question.clue: An opponent of this organization was the first cabinet appointee to be rejected by the Senate, after his recess appointment expired.

swap.leadin: Decades before becoming President, this man wrote the Braintree Instructions to oppose the Stamp Act.
swap.text: Name this second President of the United States.
swap.answerHtml: John Adams [prompt on Adams; do not accept “John Quincy Adams”]
swap.clue: This man said "facts are stubborn things" during his defense of John Preston for his role in the Boston Massacre.

question.leadin: Horace Greeley's book The American Conflict was the first to claim that this politician exclaimed "John Marshall has made his decision; now let him enforce it!"
question.text: Name this president who disregarded the Supreme Court's ruling in Worcester v. Georgia. A policy enacted by this president was continued by the signing of the Treaty of New Echota under his successor.
question.clue: Chemical exposure from paint may have led Richard Lawrence to fire two pistols, both of which failed, at this man.

swap.text: The earthquakes may have been felt as far away as Washington, D.C., where this president was preparing for the War of 1812. This shortest president drafted the Bill of Rights and succeeded Thomas Jefferson.
swap.clue: In another essay, this politician wrote that "Ambition must be made to counteract ambition," and "If men were angels, no government would be necessary."

question.leadin: Name these other people involved in the 1824 election.
question.text: The fourth place finisher, he threw his support to Adams in return for an appointment as Secretary of State.
question.clue: His first attempt to implement the American System was when this man and John Calhoun passed the Tariff of 1816.

swap.text: This member of the Lemhi Shoshone tribe joined the Lewis and Clark Expedition with her husband, Toussaint Charbonneau. Her knowledge of sign language helped her secure horses for the expedition.
swap.clue: After a group of explorers identified Cameahwait as this figure's long-lost brother, he gifted horses to those explorers.

question.leadin: Answer the following about American jurisprudence.
question.text: Much jurisprudence concerns itself with interpretations of this document and its meaning. Original intent approaches seek to interpret this document from its framers' perspective.
question.clue: This document that was amended by the Bill of Rights.

swap.text: Though American commodore Oliver Hazard Perry lost his flagship, he won the battle aboard the Niagara, defeating the British command of six ships under Robert Perry in the namesake Great Lake.
swap.clue: The Lawrence was captured twice during this battle, forcing one officer to row to another vessel while under fire.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about controversy over American neutrality between Jeffersonians and Hamiltonians.
question.text: This man sparked an international incident when he asked for a suspension of American neutrality in support of France. George Washington granted this [emphasize] "Citizen" asylum after he arrived in Philadelphia.
question.clue: This man's attempt to raise a militia for the invasion of Spanish Florida nearly led George Washington to deport him.

swap.leadin: This case grew out of goods purchased on credit from Robert Farquhar and his exectuor's attempts to collect the money he was owed.
swap.text: Identify this case, which resulted in a verdict against a Southern state and in favor of a resident of South Carolina. The rationale for the verdict was found in Article III, section 2 of the Constitution.
swap.clue: The plaintiff, a South Carolinian, sued the defendant for failing to pay him for goods purchased during the Revolutionary War. This 1793 decision held that cases against states must be tried in federal court. For 15 points-name this case which led to a ban on private lawsuits against states in the Eleventh Amendment.

question.leadin: An explosion during a battle named for this place was heard more than one hundred miles away in Pensacola.
question.text: Name this fort garrisoned by escaped slaves that was obliterated when a heated cannonball landed in its powder magazine. Andrew Jackson's destruction of this fort marks the beginning of the First Seminole War.
question.clue: This fort built by the British in Florida near Georgia was a refuge for runaway slaves, who stayed after the British left in 1815. Garcon led the defense of this fort when it was destroyed in 1816 by U.S. troops under Duncan Clinch.

swap.text: The Ute allied with the US government in a push to suppress this religious group. This group was led by Brigham Young during an 1857 campaign nicknamed "Buchanan's Blunder."
swap.clue: The massacre was perpetrated by Paiute Native Americans and members of this religious group founded by Joseph Smith. This group mostly settled in Utah.

question.text: This governor of Pennsylvania sent the militia to stop Fries' men and arrest those who would not pay the tax; he also called out the militia during the Whiskey Rebellion.

swap.leadin: The initial concession granted to this man required that all the settlers he recruited be Catholic, which he ensured by having them all take fraudulent oaths.
swap.text: Name this empresario who led the "Old Three Hundred" and was opposed by Lucas Aleman, provoking him to support Santa Anna's rebellion.
swap.clue: This man lost his country's first presidential election to the hero of the Battle of San Jacinto, Sam Houston.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Matt Lafer's favorite massacre in the whole wide world.
question.text: Peter McQueen led this murder of white settlers at the namesake location in Alabama in 1813.
question.clue: Earlier in the Creek War, a party of Red Sticks under William Weatherford and Peter McQueen had ambushed white and mixed-blood settlers under Dixon Bailey in this massacre.

swap.text: A Seneca Falls resident at the time of the convention, this woman attended it and was inspired to start her own feminist publication, The Lily, which promoted reformed fashion advice and temperance.
swap.clue: This reformer published the first newspaper edited entirely by women, the temperance journal The Lily.
